metadata.title: Chinese Test Corpus
metadata.notes: Test fixture. Two Aesop fables and a repetition text, written in English for this fixture and machine-translated into Mandarin with Google Translate; the Mandarin is the corpus text and the English originals are the sentence translations. Word segmentation: jieba, hand-corrected.

sentences.text: 一个炎热的下午，一只饥饿的狐狸走过花园。

translations.text: One hot afternoon a hungry fox walked through a garden.

sentences.text: 他看到一串成熟的葡萄挂在高高的藤蔓上。

translations.text: He saw a bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a high vine.

sentences.text: 狐狸跳了起来，但他够不到葡萄。

translations.text: The fox jumped up, but he could not reach the grapes.

sentences.text: 他一次又一次地尝试，但还是够不到他们。

translations.text: He tried again and again, and still he could not reach them.

sentences.text: 最后狐狸走开了，并说那些葡萄是酸的。

translations.text: At last the fox walked away and said that those grapes were sour.
The fox ran to the river.
The fox ran to the river.

sentences.text: 狐狸喝了水，然后狐狸又喝了水。

translations.text: The fox drank water, and then the fox drank water again.

sentences.text: 一只小狐狸和一只大狐狸坐在河边。

translations.text: A small fox and a big fox sat by the river.
